identity.name: TrackMan Intelligence
identity.goal: Drive fitting bookings and coaching sessions

visualDirection.mood: Clinical precision. Data权威. TrackMan blue dominance.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: TrackMan data is the hero. Numbers, charts, launch monitor visuals. Chrome golf clubs on dark backgrounds. PGA Tour stat comparisons. Clean, scientific, premium. Think golf analytics lab meets luxury sports brand.
imageReferences: TrackMan launch monitor screen with ball flight data
Chrome iron head with data overlay (TrackMan numbers)
Golfer swing capture with split-screen stat comparison
visualDirection.colorUsage: Use TrackMan blue (#0066CC) as dominant brand colour. Green (#00CC77) for positive metrics and CTAs. Gold for pricing. Never use for backgrounds — text only. Keep dark backgrounds consistent.
visualDirection.typography: Roboto Condensed Bold for numbers and headlines. Inter for body. Monospace for data labels.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Split screen: product/club on left, TrackMan data overlay on right. Dark backgrounds throughout. Numbers should dominate the visual hierarchy.
contentExamples: Your drive: 217m. PGA Tour avg: 264m. TrackMan found the gap.
Launch monitor screenshot showing spin rate + carry distance

brief.purpose: Drive fitting bookings and coaching sessions by proving Swing Shack's TrackMan technology gives golfers data-driven insight their game has been missing.
brief.audience: Jozi golfers, 25-50, mid-high handicap. They track their fitness — they want to track their golf. Data-aware, skeptical of voodoo tips, willing to pay for evidence-based improvement.
brief.bigIdea: Your swing has a number. TrackMan measures it. That number is the shortcut to better scores.
brief.successMetric: Fitting sessions booked. Secondary: GMB posts live weekly. Tertiary: engagement rate on stat-hook content above 2.5%.
brief.whatGoodLooksLike: A hook that stops the scroll with a specific number. A visual that shows TrackMan data overlaid on a club or swing. A caption that earns the click by expanding the data story. Booking link front and centre.
brief.whatBadLooksLike: Vague transformation claims ('From confused golfer to confident striker'). Busy backgrounds without contrast. Price-led content without data justification. Anything that looks like generic golf marketing.

dna.tone: Clinical authority. Data speaks, we just translate it. No hype, no fluff — numbers are the argument. Authoritative but not cold. Expert without being gatekeeping.
dna.contentMix: 70% educational (data insights, stats explainers) / 20% promotional (session offers, fitting deals) / 10% social proof (client results, before/after)
forbiddenVisualStyles: text over busy backgrounds without contrast layer
dna.ctaPhilosophy: Direct price-led with anchoring: show the value first (TrackMan data), then introduce the offer. Always include R-amount. 'From R250' works because the data has already justified the price.

platformStrategy.instagram: Stat-first hook stops the scroll. Data overlay on image tells the story. Caption expands with context. Link in bio drives booking.
platformStrategy.tiktok: Hook is the number/stat itself. 'Your drive: 199m' as text overlay. 3-second hook, then explain the data. Fast-cut, punchy.
platformStrategy.gmb: Trust + proof + convenience. Service highlight with one key stat. Clean, professional, no gimmicks. Call to action is always 'book now' or 'call us'.

exampleHighPerforming.whyItWorked: 'Your golf stats don't lie' — specific, implies measurement, triggers curiosity about what the stats reveal. Stats hooks 2.5x better than transformation hooks.

exampleLowPerforming.whyItFailed: 'FROM CONFUSED GOLFER TO CONFIDENT STRIKER' — vague, no data anchor. Transformation claims without proof feel empty.

bestHooks.notes: Stats angle consistently outperforms transformation. 'Your [metric]' format is the winner.

failedContent.reason: Vague transformation claim, no data anchor
failedContent.lesson: Always lead with a number or specific stat. 'Your [X]' outperforms 'FROM [state] TO [state]'
Weather/indoor convenience is table stakes, not a hook. Stats create urgency.

lessonsLearned: Stats hooks consistently outperform all other angles — lead with numbers always
Meters > Yards for SA market — confirmed April 2026
Dark background with data overlay looks premium with TrackMan theme
Caption ≠ Overlay Text — supplementary copy drives click-through, not the hook itself
Hook A best performer (Round 1) was never re-published — opportunity cost

strategy.targetAudience: Jozi golfers, 25-50, mid-high handicap, data-aware. Already tracking fitness — they want to track golf too.
strategy.primaryOffer: TrackMan Assessment from R900. First session R250. Bundle R1,400 (save R250)

identity.name: Takomo 101T

visualDirection.mood: Premium hollow-body iron. Chrome silver. Understated power. Value-driven but not cheap.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Takomo 101T chrome iron on dark backgrounds. Price transparency is a hook — show the value. Sleek, blade-like aesthetics. Target: serious golfers who do research before buying. Clean product shots with minimal data. The iron should look desirable on its own merits, not needing TrackMan to sell it.

Irons laid out in bag — clean product photography
Swing Shack fitting session with Takomo irons (real photo)

visualDirection.typography: Helvetica Neue Bold for headlines. Clean sans for body. Price callouts in gold, bold.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Product hero: full iron head on pure black. Price callout overlaid in gold. Tagline below. No TrackMan data on product shots — keep it pure product photography.

Takomo 101T — the iron that divides serious golfers

brief.purpose: Establish Takomo 101T as the smart golfer's iron of choice in SA — premium hollow-body technology at a price that challenges the big brands.
brief.audience: Serious golfers, 25-50, mid-to-low handicap. They do their research. They want Tour-level performance without Tour-level prices. They read reviews, compare specs, and buy based on data not branding.
brief.bigIdea: Takomo 101T: the iron that gets serious golfers arguing — and fitting sessions that settle the argument.
brief.successMetric: Takomo fitting sessions booked. Secondary: engagement on Takomo content above TrackMan benchmark. Tertiary: Takomo mentions in bio link clicks.
brief.whatGoodLooksLike: A real Takomo iron head on pure black — no AI, no stock photos. A price callout in gold that creates urgency without discounting. A hook that poses a question serious golfers want answered. Copy that respects the reader's intelligence.
brief.whatBadLooksLike: AI-generated club heads that look fake. Broken/garbled text. Price claims without the 'under $600' anchor. Generic golf content that could be any iron. Anything that talks down to the audience.

dna.tone: Confident, curious, slightly provocative. The kind of content that makes serious golfers stop and think — then book a fitting to settle the argument. Sharp without being aggressive.
dna.contentMix: 50% product education (what makes Takomo different) / 30% controversy/question angle / 20% value proof (price-to-performance)
preferredVisualStyles: real product photography of Takomo iron head on black
clean product cutout on dark background
gold price callout overlaid on chrome
forbiddenVisualStyles: AI-generated club/product heads (Christelle rule) — real product photography only
busy backgrounds with text overlay without contrast layer
stock golf photos without product context
dna.ctaPhilosophy: Price transparency as hook: lead with 'less than $600' or 'from R250' because the value is the argument. CTAs are always 'Book Takomo Fitting' with R-amount anchored.

platformStrategy.instagram: Product-first: the iron head IS the hero. Price callout in gold. Caption earns the click with the controversy/question angle. Link to booking.
platformStrategy.tiktok: Hook is the price question: 'Is Takomo 101T worth it? We put it on TrackMan.' Product visual first, data second.
platformStrategy.gmb: Takomo fitting service highlight. Price-led. Trust signal: 'Swing Shack is authorized Takomo fitter.'

exampleLowPerforming.whyItFailed: AI-generated club head looked fake. Text broken/garbled. Pricing callout wrong. Product credibility too low. Real product photography required per Christelle gate rule.

failedContent.reason: AI product imagery looks fake. Broken text. Wrong pricing. Product credibility too low.
failedContent.lesson: Golf club/physical product campaigns require real product photography. AI may only do background/layout/text treatment. No AI product heads.

lessonsLearned: For golf clubs and physical products: requiresRealProductImage = true always
AI-generated club heads fail Gate 2 by default
Text must be added as separate design layer — never embedded in generated image
Broken text = automatic quality gate failure

identity.name: Winter Golf
identity.goal: Drive indoor golf sessions during SA winter season

visualDirection.mood: Cozy indoor warmth vs cold outside. Jozi winter contrast. Indoor golf paradise.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Cold outside, warm inside. The contrast between grey Jo'burg winter and the warmth, green satisfaction of indoor golf. Pizzas, beers, premium simulators. Social golf atmosphere. NOT about technique or data — about the experience and enjoyment. Think: pub golf meets luxury simulator.
imageReferences: Simulator screen showing lush course in winter grey context
Cozy indoor setup with warm lighting
Post-round drinks at Swing Shack bar
Rain on window outside, golfer smiling inside
visualDirection.colorUsage: Cool blues for winter theme (#4A90D9). Warm accent for indoor coziness (#D4A574 or warm amber). Never clinical — keep it inviting and social.
visualDirection.typography: Warm, approachable. Bold for contrast headlines. Friendly sans-serif.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Split mood: grey/cold outside vs warm/green inside. Social proof. Food and beverage welcome. Not data-heavy.
contentExamples: It's 8°C outside. 22°C inside. Your game never stops.
Rain check? How about a round.

brief.purpose: Keep Swing Shack bookings steady through SA winter by positioning indoor golf as the obvious choice when outdoor courses go cold.
brief.audience: Regular Jo'burg golfers who stop playing in winter because their home course gets cold or they travel less. They already have clubs — they just need a reason to keep playing.
brief.bigIdea: Winter doesn't exist in here. (It's always 22°C, there's food and drinks, and the simulator never closes.)
brief.successMetric: Winter session bookings vs prior year. Secondary: winter package upsells. Tertiary: social engagement on contrast-style content.
brief.whatGoodLooksLike: A visual that makes you want to be inside — warm lights, green fairways on screen, something cold and grey outside the window. A hook that names the weather or the day. Content that feels like a friend saying 'actually, this is good.'
brief.whatBadLooksLike: Clinical data overlays. Golf swing technique photos. Anything that makes indoor golf sound like a chore or a substitute. Content that positions winter as a problem rather than Swing Shack as the answer.

dna.tone: Warm, inviting, slightly cheeky. The tone of a friend who knows the best spot in Jo'burg. Not trying to be premium or clinical — just genuinely fun. Think: 'you know what this weather needs? A round.'
dna.contentMix: 40% social proof (look how good it is inside) / 30% contrast/humor (cold vs warm) / 20% practical (sessions available, deals) / 10% lifestyle (food, drinks, atmosphere)
preferredVisualStyles: cozy bar/food setup at Swing Shack
contrast: grey sky outside vs green simulator inside
forbiddenVisualStyles: cold blue colour grading on indoor content
anything that makes indoor golf look like a chore
dna.ctaPhilosophy: Casual and low-friction: 'Book a session' not 'Book now — limited slots.' Make it feel like a no-brainer, not a sales push.

platformStrategy.instagram: Lifestyle-first: food, drinks, simulators, social vibe. Contrast hooks work well. Carousels showing 'inside vs outside' perform.
platformStrategy.tiktok: 'It's [X]°C outside. This is what we did instead.' Fast, relatable, shareable. Show the vibe, not the data.
platformStrategy.gmb: Seasonal/event posts. 'Winter sessions available.' Warm imagery, social proof. 'Book your winter round.'

strategy.positioningStatement: When the courses go cold, the simulator doesn't.
strategy.targetAudience: Regular Jo'burg golfers who play less in winter. They love golf but the weather stops them.
strategy.primaryOffer: Winter sessions from R250. Winter package deals available.

pillars.name: Social
pillars.description: Food, drinks, company — make it a round

brief.audience: Johannesburg golfers who are using ill-suited clubs, struggling with consistency, or looking to improve their game through better equipment choices.
brief.goalNotes: Drive practice session and fitting bookings by educating golfers on the importance of using the correct clubs for their swing, skill level, and playing style. Reinforce that the right equipment leads to better performance, consistency, and enjoyment on the course.
brief.context: Campaign theme: "You wouldn't dig a hole with a pool noodle. You wouldn't run a marathon in flip-flops. So why play golf with the wrong clubs?" Visual direction should compare obviously incorrect tools or equipment with golfers using unsuitable clubs. Focus on education, performance improvement, and the value of proper club selection and fitting.

strategy.positioningStatement: For Johannesburg golfers who are using ill-suited clubs, struggling with consistency, or looking to improve their game through better equipment choices. who want to Bookings.
strategy.targetAudience: Johannesburg golfers who are using ill-suited clubs, struggling with consistency, or looking to improve their game through better equipment choices.

pillars.name: The Absurdity Principle — Wrong Tool Comparisons
pillars.description: Owns the campaign's core tension by making the ridiculous obvious. Uses vivid, relatable comparisons that force recognition — if it's absurd in other contexts, it's absurd on the course. This pillar creates the initial awareness and emotional hook.

pillars.name: The Hidden Performance Cost — What Wrong Equipment Steals
pillars.description: Owns the educational proof of impact. Shows specific ways ill-suited clubs damage performance: inconsistent contact, lost distance, unnecessary spin, compensations that create bad habits. This pillar provides the logical justification for the emotional hook.

pillars.name: The Fitting Revelation — Science Meets Art
pillars.description: Owns the 'aha moment' content — demystifying what club fitting actually is and why it matters. Shows the process, the technology, the expertise. Positions fitting as the solution discovered, not a service sold. Builds trust and removes objections.

pillars.name: The Transformation Proof — Real Results, Real Golfers
pillars.description: Owns social proof and credibility. Features Johannesburg golfers whose game changed after proper fitting. Shows measurable improvements, emotional reactions, and specific outcomes. Makes the abstract benefit concrete and local.

pillars.name: The Invitation — Book Your Practice Session
pillars.description: Owns the conversion moment. Every piece of content leads here — not as a hard sell but as the natural next step after revelation. Presents booking as the path to discovery, not just a transaction. Makes the CTA feel like self-improvement, not spending.

dna.tone: Confrontational empathy — a provocative wake-up call that makes golfers question their equipment choices while feeling empowered to change
dna.contentMix: 35% comparison/contrast / 30% educational / 20% social proof / 15% direct response
dna.ctaPhilosophy: The CTA should feel like the natural next step after a realization — not pushy but inviting. 'Book Your Fitting' or 'Get Your Practice Session' positions the booking as the solution discovered, not a sales ask.

platformStrategy.instagram: Use carousel posts for the comparison narrative (swipe to see wrong vs right), Reels for dramatic before/after swing comparisons, and Stories for polling audience about their equipment doubts. GMB posts should be educational with clear booking CTAs integrated into the value proposition.
platformStrategy.tiktok: N/A for this campaign — focus all energy on Instagram and GMB where golfer intent is highest.
platformStrategy.gmb: Optimize posts for local search intent. Use educational content that answers 'why does equipment matter' with a natural CTA to book. Showcase fitting process and results to build trust for the primary offer.

visualDirection.mood: Dramatic revelation meets empowering solution — like a lightbulb moment on a dark course
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Visuals should create immediate cognitive dissonance. Open with obviously wrong scenarios — a chef trying to flip sushi with a baseball bat, a surgeon using butter knives — then cut to a golfer struggling with clubs that are clearly wrong for their swing. The contrast must be jarring. Then pivot: show the moment of discovery when the right equipment is introduced, culminating in the gold-accented reveal of proper fitting. Every visual should tell the story of mismatch becoming match.
imageReferences: chef attempting precision work with oversized cleaver against pristine white tablecloth
golfer mid-swing with clubs visibly too long/short for their frame in dramatic lighting
fitter hands holding correctly-matched club against dark background with gold accent lighting
client reaction shot — moment of realization when perfect club meets correct swing
visualDirection.colorUsage: The dark background (#0D0D0F) creates the dramatic stage — it makes the warm orange (#FF6B35) feel urgent and impossible to ignore, like a warning light. The gold accent (#D4AF37) is reserved exclusively for the solution moments — the right club, the fitting appointment, the successful shot. This creates a psychological pattern: orange = problem identified, gold = problem solved. White text ensures readability against the dark canvas and maintains the premium, confident tone.
visualDirection.typography: Bold, high-contrast sans-serif for headlines — something that commands attention and delivers the provocative message. Use uppercase for the comparison statements ('WRONG TOOL') to create visual urgency. Body text should be clean and readable, contrasting the dramatic headlines.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Strong vertical hierarchy: bold statement at top, supporting visual below, CTA anchored at bottom. Use negative space strategically — the dark background IS the layout element. Carousel posts should use consistent frames with progressive revelation. Each slide advances the narrative from problem to solution.
contentExamples: Carousel: 'You wouldn't run a marathon in flip-flops. So why play golf with clubs that don't match your swing?' — swipe to reveal the answer
Reel: Split-screen comparison of same golfer using wrong clubs vs correctly fitted clubs, same swing, dramatically different results
Educational post: '3 signs your clubs are holding you back (and you don't even know it)' with infographic
Client transformation: 'After 20 years of inconsistent shots, one fitting session changed everything' with swing comparison
